questions.stem: Which of the following lists metals in order from most reactive to least reactive?
questions.explanation: The correct order from most reactive to least reactive is Sodium (Na), Magnesium (Mg), Iron (Fe), Copper (Cu). In the reactivity series, the order runs K, Na, Li, Ca, Mg, Al, Zn, Fe, Cu, Ag, Au, Pt.

questions.stem: Why is potassium more reactive than sodium?

options.text: Potassium has fewer electron shells, so the outer electron is closer to the nucleus
Potassium has a smaller atomic radius and stronger nuclear attraction
Potassium has more electron shells, so its outer electron is further from the nucleus and lost more easily
Potassium has more protons, which repel the outer electron more strongly

questions.explanation: Potassium has more electron shells than sodium, meaning the outer electron is further from the nucleus. There is also more shielding from inner electrons. This makes the outer electron easier to lose, making potassium more reactive.
